title: OK Computer
label: Parlophone
tagline: Twelve songs about cars, computers, politicians and the low hum of modern anxiety, recorded in a rehearsal shed and an old manor house near Bath. The record where Radiohead stopped being 'the band that did Creep'.
sessionsText: After the success of The Bends, Radiohead decided to record without a studio deadline. They started in Canned Applause, their rehearsal space near Didcot, with Nigel Godrich producing, then moved into St Catherine's Court, a historic house outside Bath, where the rooms themselves became part of the sound.

lineupHeadline:
Five players.
One voice from a Mac.

tracks.title: Airbag
tracks.note: A song about surviving a car crash. Phil Selway's drums were cut up and rearranged on a computer, inspired by the sampled beats of DJ Shadow.

tracks.title: Paranoid Android
tracks.note: Several song fragments stitched together, in the spirit of the Beatles' Happiness Is a Warm Gun. The title borrows Marvin, the gloomy robot from The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy.

tracks.title: Subterranean Homesick Alien
tracks.note: The title nods to Bob Dylan's Subterranean Homesick Blues. The narrator dreams of being taken away by aliens, then imagines nobody believing him.

tracks.title: Exit Music (For a Film)
tracks.note: Written for Baz Luhrmann's Romeo + Juliet and played over its end credits. It starts with just voice and acoustic guitar and swells into distorted bass and drums.

tracks.title: Let Down
tracks.note: Recorded in the early hours in the ballroom at St Catherine's Court. Jonny Greenwood's chiming guitar pattern runs in a different meter from the rest of the band.

tracks.title: Karma Police
tracks.note: The name began as a band in-joke on tour. A piano-led song that collapses at the end into a wash of guitar feedback.

tracks.title: Fitter Happier
tracks.note: No singing at all: a list of self-improvement slogans read by 'Fred', a synthetic voice built into Apple Macintosh computers, over piano and samples.

tracks.title: Electioneering
tracks.note: The loudest, most straightforward rock song on the record, about politics and selling out. Listen for the cowbell.

tracks.title: Climbing Up the Walls
tracks.note: The album's darkest moment. Jonny Greenwood wrote the strings to slide between notes a quarter-tone apart, taking his cue from the Polish composer Krzysztof Penderecki.

tracks.title: No Surprises
tracks.note: A lullaby led by glockenspiel. The gentle sound sits against a lyric about a quiet, deadening routine.

tracks.title: Lucky
tracks.note: The first OK Computer song to be finished, recorded in a single day for The Help Album, a War Child charity record raising money for victims of the war in Bosnia.

tracks.title: The Tourist
tracks.note: Written by Jonny Greenwood after watching tourists rush through a French town to see everything at once. A plea to slow down, ending on a single ding of a bell.

world.what: Labour wins a landslide in the UK general election and Tony Blair becomes prime minister.
IBM's Deep Blue computer beats world chess champion Garry Kasparov in a full match for the first time.
Hong Kong returns to Chinese sovereignty, on the same day OK Computer comes out in the US.
Diana, Princess of Wales, dies in a car crash in Paris.

trivia: The title comes from a line in the radio version of The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, which the band listened to on the tour bus.
Radiohead's headline set at Glastonbury in June 1997 was plagued by technical problems, and Yorke nearly walked off. It is now often ranked among the festival's greatest performances.
In 2015 the US Library of Congress added OK Computer to its National Recording Registry of culturally significant recordings.
For the 20th anniversary in 2017, the band released OKNOTOK, adding three songs from the era that had never been officially released: I Promise, Man of War and Lift.

quiz.question: Where did Radiohead record most of OK Computer?
quiz.explanation: St Catherine's Court, a historic house outside Bath, after early sessions in their rehearsal shed near Didcot.

quiz.question: Exit Music (For a Film) was written for which movie?
quiz.explanation: Baz Luhrmann's Romeo + Juliet, where it plays over the end credits.

quiz.question: Who 'reads' Fitter Happier?
options: A synthetic voice from a Macintosh
quiz.explanation: 'Fred', one of the text-to-speech voices built into Apple's Macintosh computers.
